newsitem.title: NORWAY: Sluggish Norwegian shares pause after bull run.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish Norwegian shares pause after bull run.

text.p: Norwegian shares took a small step downwards on Thursday in sluggish trade, but dealers said they saw little propect of a major correction, unless there was a slide in the United States or on European markets.
Oslo's Total share index retreated 0.2 percent to close at 1,262.55 points in turnover of 665 million crowns.
"Norway's a little sluggish today because of the bull run yesterday, people are saying it was going slightly too fast," said a broker.
He added that a rise in official interest rates a day ago may also have contributed to investors putting on the brakes.
"They ignored the rate hike but now they're figuring out what it means. But investors still have cash and if the market were to come off, there's cash there to buy it back up."

Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) surged 6.8 percent to 94 crowns led by a 7.8 percent jump on the Copenhagen bourse after Britain's NatWest analysts forecast a 40 percent rise in the share price in the next year.

Tanker company Frontline Ltd FRO.OL rose 4.7 percent to 33.50 crowns in turnover of 41 million crowns. Frontline has risen almost 17 percent compared with the closing price on July 7, when it was launched on the bourse.
